claims.claim: groundwater supplies 55 % of inflow at Walden Pond, Massachusetts (Colman & Friesz 2001)
claims.location: p. 17 (PDF p. 17), Water-Balance Results and Fig. 9; abstract, p. 1
claims.quote: whereas ground-water inflow contributed about 55 percent of the inflow
claims.conditions: average annual water budget for 1995–99; Walden Pond is a 24.88-ha glacial kettle lake with NO surface inlet or outlet, so the other 45 % is precipitation falling on the lake surface (1.215 m/yr); groundwater inflow 1.47 m/yr (366,000 m³/yr) is the mean of a contributing-area estimate (1.35 m/yr) and an isotope mass-balance estimate (1.59 m/yr); outflow 74 % seepage to groundwater, 26 % evaporation; residence time 4.8 yr
claims.note: Right as stated. For the comparison with Hot Brook it is worth saying that Walden has no streams at all, so its 55 % is groundwater against direct precipitation only; a stream-fed lake's groundwater share would be smaller.
